name: Sunlit Salt Water Curse Breaking
description: This is the completely non-toxic way to break a curse: it uses only water, sea salt, lemon, sunlight, a white or LED candle and your own words, with nothing burned that makes smoke and nothing poisonous. Salt and water are among the most widespread cleansing agents in folk practice, and many traditions treat sunlight as a natural purifier that burns away what is hidden. The salt water draws the curse out, the sun clears it, and pouring it away carries it off for good. It is gentle enough to do with children and pets in the house.

ingredients.item: White candle or white LED candle
Bright sunny windowsill or outdoor spot
Your own spoken words of release

steps: Choose a bright morning and wash the glass bowl, then fill it with the fresh water.
Stir in the sea salt clockwise three times until it dissolves, saying, 'Salt of the sea, make this water clean.'
Float the Lemon slices on top; in many folk traditions the sour, bright lemon is said to cut through and absorb heavy or crossed energy.
Set the bowl in direct sunlight and place the white candle or LED candle beside it; an LED candle keeps the spell completely smoke-free and flame-free.
Hold your hands over the bowl without touching the water and say, in your own words, what has felt cursed or heavy and that you now release it.
Speak the chant three times, then leave the bowl in the sun for at least three hours while the light works on it.
In the afternoon, put out or switch off the candle and pour the water down the sink with the tap running, or onto bare gravel or pavement away from plants, saying, 'It is gone and I am free.'
Put the lemon slices in the trash or compost, wash the bowl, and wash your hands.
howToUse: Repeat for three sunny days in a row if the curse or heavy feeling has lasted a long time. Afterward, open the curtains in your home each morning for a week to let the sun keep working. The candle and bowl can be reused once washed.
chant:
Salt of sea and light of sun,
what was cast is now undone.
Water, take it, lemon, clear,
no curse may stay or linger here.
intention: I release every curse and heavy influence on me, and the sun and sea make me clean and free.
timing: Sunday (the Sun's day) around midday; waning moon to remove, or any sunny day when needed.
bestTime: Any season with strong sun; especially late spring and summer.
caution: This is the non-toxic option: nothing is burned, smoked, eaten or applied to the skin. If you use a real candle instead of the LED candle: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Lemon juice on skin followed by sunlight can cause a blistering burn-like rash (phytophotodermatitis), so handle the lemon slices with clean hands, wash your hands before going into the sun, and keep the juice off your skin. Keep the bowl where small children cannot tip it over. Pour salt water away from garden plants and lawns, since salt harms them. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk; do not drink the salt water.
pets: Lemons are listed by the ASPCA as toxic to dogs and cats, and salt water can cause salt poisoning, so set the bowl where pets cannot drink from it or chew the slices.

name: Nine Knots Unbinding to Break a Curse
description: Knot magic is found across European folk practice, where tying knots was believed to bind luck, weather, health or ill will, and untying them was believed to release it. This curse breaker works in reverse of a binding: you tie the curse into nine knots, then patiently untie every one by candlelight, unraveling its hold on you. Unlike cord cutting, which severs a tie in one stroke, this method takes the curse apart piece by piece and leaves the cord whole and clean.

ingredients.item: Black cotton cord or string, about 18 inches

steps: Place the white candle in a sturdy holder on the heatproof dish and light it, asking for clarity and release.
Hold the black cord and think of the curse, bad influence or crossed condition you want broken.
Tie nine loose knots along the cord, spacing them evenly; with each one, name an effect of the curse (bad luck, worry, blocked money, and so on). Keep them loose so they can be untied.
Hold the knotted cord near (never over) the candle flame's light and speak the chant once.
Starting from the last knot you tied, untie each knot in turn, saying, 'This knot is loosed, this hold is gone,' until the cord is smooth again.
Stir the sea salt and Rosemary into the bowl of water, then dip the cord in it three times to wash away what was tied in it.
Let the candle burn for at least 15 more minutes while you sit quietly, then snuff it out.
howToUse: Let the cord dry, then either bury it off your property or keep it, now clean, as a reminder that the curse has no hold. Pour the salt water down the drain with the tap running. Relight the candle for a few minutes each night until it is used up, while repeating the chant once.
chant:
Knot by knot I set me free,
no spell nor curse has hold on me.
What was bound is loosed and gone,
the cord is clean, I carry on.
intention: I untie every hold that a curse or ill wish has had on me, one knot at a time.
timing: Saturday or Tuesday during a waning moon.
bestTime: Autumn, the natural season of letting go; or any time needed.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep the cord well away from the flame; never hold it over or in the candle, as cotton cord catches fire easily. Keep loose cord away from young children and pets, as it is a strangling and swallowing hazard. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk; do not drink the salt water.
pets: String and cord swallowed by cats and dogs can cause dangerous intestinal blockages, and salt water can cause salt poisoning; keep both out of reach and put the cord away after use.

name: Return to Sender Box to Break a Curse
description: Returning harm to its source, often called 'return to sender' work in modern folk magic and hoodoo-influenced practice, uses mirrors because a mirror sends back whatever faces it. This curse breaker seals the curse inside a small mirrored box, where it is turned around and sent home transformed into harmless light, so that it hurts no one, including the sender. Where a mirror shield guards you against what is coming, this box catches what has already landed and sends it back neutralized.

ingredients.item: Small cardboard or wooden box with a lid
Self-adhesive acrylic mirror tiles or craft mirror sheet (shatterproof), or aluminum foil shiny side out
Tape or string to seal the box

steps: Line the inside of the box and lid with the acrylic mirror or foil, reflective side facing inward.
Light the white candle in a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish nearby, away from the box and paper.
On the paper write: 'Whatever harm was sent to me returns to its source as harmless light, harming none.' Do not write anyone's name; the spell finds its own way back.
Fold the paper away from you three times and place it in the box.
Sprinkle in the sea salt, then add the Black Tourmaline and Bay Laurel leaf to absorb and seal.
Close the lid, say the chant three times, and seal the box with tape or tie it shut with string.
Snuff the candle when you are done, or let it burn while you sit with it, then put it out before leaving the room.
howToUse: Keep the sealed box in a dark, out-of-the-way place such as a closet shelf for one full moon cycle. Then open it, put the paper and salt in the trash outside your home, cleanse the stone in moonlight, and recycle or burn the box safely outdoors in a fire pit if local rules allow. You can reuse the mirror lining for future boxes.
chant:
Mirror bright and mirror true,
what was sent comes back from you.
Turned to light, it harms no one,
the curse goes home, and it is done.
intention: I send every curse or ill wish aimed at me back to its source as harmless light, harming none.
timing: Saturday during a waning or dark moon.
bestTime: Any time of year, as soon as you sense harm sent your way.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Use shatterproof acrylic mirror or foil rather than glass; if you use glass mirror pieces, tape every edge and wear gloves. Keep the box and loose stones away from young children, as small stones are a choking hazard. Never burn the box indoors. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Bay Laurel is listed by the ASPCA as toxic to dogs, cats and horses, and small stones can be swallowed; keep the box sealed and out of reach.

name: Hyssop and Salt Head Wash to Break a Curse
description: Hyssop holds a central place in hoodoo uncrossing work, rooted in Psalm 51:7, 'Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean,' which is often prayed while washing. This curse breaker is a quick head wash rather than a full bath: a cooled hyssop tea with a little salt is poured from the crown of the head downward, carrying the crossed condition off the body and down the drain. It is useful when you have no tub or need fast relief.
steps: Pour the boiling water over the dried Hyssop in the pitcher, cover, and steep for 15 minutes.
Strain out every bit of herb, stir in the sea salt until dissolved, and let the wash cool completely to lukewarm or room temperature; test it on your wrist.
Do a patch test first: dab a little on your inner arm and wait 15 minutes. Do not continue if you see redness or itching.
Light the white candle in a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish in the bathroom, well away from towels and curtains.
Stand or kneel in the shower or tub, close your eyes tightly, and pray Psalm 51 or speak the chant.
Pour the wash slowly over the crown of your head and let it run down your body, always pouring downward to push the curse off and away.
Pat dry with the white towel rather than rubbing, then put on clean, light-colored clothes and snuff the candle.
howToUse: Many practitioners do this wash for three, seven or nine days in a row, making a fresh batch each time. Collect a little of the used water from the tub if you like and pour it out at a crossroads or onto the street, walking away without looking back; otherwise let it all go down the drain. Rinse your hair with plain water afterward if salt leaves it dry.
chant:
Hyssop green and salt of sea,
wash this crossing off of me.
Crown to foot and down the drain,
I stand uncrossed and clean again.
intention: I wash every curse and crossed condition from my head and body and stand clean and free.
timing: At sunrise; Thursday or Sunday; waning moon to remove.
bestTime: Any season; especially at the turn of the year or after a run of trouble.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep the candle out of the splash zone and away from towels. Let the wash cool fully before use to avoid scalds, keep your eyes and mouth closed, and rinse eyes with clean water if any gets in. Do a patch test first, and skip the wash on broken, sunburned or irritated skin or if you are allergic to plants in the mint family. Use only dried hyssop herb; never use Hyssop essential oil, which can cause seizures and must not be swallowed or used neat on skin. Avoid during pregnancy and with children unless a health professional approves. Keep the tub floor from getting slippery. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk; do not drink the wash.
interactions: Not taken internally. Hyssop taken by mouth may interact with seizure medicines and is not recommended in pregnancy, which is one more reason never to drink the wash.
pets: Keep the wash and the leftover herbs away from pets, and do not let them drink from the tub or pitcher, as salt water can cause salt poisoning.

name: Rosemary and Bay Bundle to Seal a Curse Break
description: After a curse is broken, many practitioners seal the work so nothing new can come in. Rosemary has long been hung at doorways in English and Mediterranean folklore to keep out evil, and bay laurel has a reputation in European lore as a protective plant. This smoke-free curse breaker binds them into a door bundle with red thread and pairs it with a small salt jar, closing the door on the old curse without burning anything and without the toxic rue found in some older recipes.

ingredients.item: Small glass jar with a lid
Small nail or adhesive hook for hanging

steps: Do this after one of your curse breaking spells, or on its own when you want to close your home to ill will.
Gather the Rosemary sprigs with the stems together and tuck the Bay Laurel leaves into the center.
Wind the red thread tightly around the stems seven times, tie three knots, and leave a loop for hanging, saying the chant as you tie.
Fill the jar with the sea salt and whole Black Pepper, stirring counterclockwise to push away what is broken, then cap it tightly.
Hold the jar and say, 'The curse is broken, the door is sealed.'
Hang the bundle high above the inside of your front door with the nail or hook, and place the salt jar on a high shelf or ledge near the door.
howToUse: Leave the bundle up to dry naturally; it keeps working for about three months or until it crumbles. Replace it with a fresh bundle each season, and compost or bury the old one with thanks. Replace the salt in the jar each time you replace the bundle, throwing the old salt in the trash outside.
chant:
Rosemary green and laurel bright,
guard this door by day and night.
The curse is broke, the way is sealed,
by thread and salt my home is healed.
intention: I seal my home and myself so that no curse may return or enter here.
timing: Saturday, waning moon to seal out harm, or right after a curse breaking.
bestTime: Any season; refresh at each solstice and equinox.
caution: This method is smoke-free and flame-free. It contains no rue, which is toxic and causes skin burns. Hang the bundle securely and well away from lamps, heaters and stove burners, since dried herbs are flammable. Keep the salt jar sealed and up high, away from children. Wash hands after handling peppercorns before touching your eyes. Bay leaves are stiff and sharp and can scratch the throat if swallowed whole, so keep the bundle and loose leaves out of reach. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Bay Laurel is listed by the ASPCA as toxic to dogs, cats and horses, and salt can cause salt poisoning; hang the bundle and store the jar where pets cannot reach fallen leaves or spilled salt. Rosemary is not considered toxic to pets.

name: Secondhand Car Clearing
description: A used car carries the history of its past owners, and in many folk traditions any secondhand item is cleansed before it is made your own. This spell clears bad luck and old energy from a newly bought used car with a thorough clean, a gentle salt water wipe and a protective herb sachet, all without flames or smoke inside the vehicle. It prepares the car for the Car Protection Charm or simply for a fresh start on the road.

ingredients.item: Spray bottle of water with a pinch of sea salt

steps: Remove everything the previous owner left behind, including old papers, air fresheners and trash.
Vacuum the seats, floors and trunk thoroughly, imagining the old luck being pulled away with the dust.

Lightly mist a cloth (never the dashboard or electronics directly) with the salt water and wipe the steering wheel, door handles and seat edges, then wipe again with a damp cloth of plain water so no salt residue remains on surfaces.
Open all the doors and ring the bell inside the car, front to back, to shake loose anything left.
Fill the sachet with the Rosemary, Bay Laurel leaf and Clear Quartz, and tie it closed while speaking the chant.
Close the doors, sit in the driver's seat, put your hands on the wheel, and say, 'This car is cleared and this car is mine.'
Tuck the sachet into the glove box or a door pocket, where it cannot slide under the pedals.
howToUse: Keep the sachet in the glove box and replace the herbs once a year or after any accident or close call. Repeat the bell clearing whenever the car feels unlucky. Dispose of old herbs in the compost or trash.
chant:
Road behind and road ahead,
old luck gone and old ties shed.
Clean and clear from wheel to door,
this car is mine forevermore.
intention: I clear this car of past owners' luck and history and claim it for safe, lucky travel.
timing: Wednesday (Mercury, travel) or Sunday, on a dry day during a waning moon.
bestTime: As soon as possible after buying the car.
caution: Never light candles, incense or herbs inside a car. Do not spray salt water on electronics, screens, airbag covers or the dashboard, and wipe off any salt so it cannot corrode metal or stain upholstery. Never leave the car running in a closed garage while you work, as exhaust contains carbon monoxide. Keep the sachet secured where it cannot fall under the pedals or block an airbag. Keep the sachet and small stone away from young children, as they are a choking hazard. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Bay Laurel is listed by the ASPCA as toxic to dogs and cats; keep the sachet in the closed glove box if pets ride in the car.

name: Secondhand Jewelry and Crystal Cleansing
description: Many people believe that jewelry and crystals hold on to the feelings of whoever owned them before, so a thrifted ring or a gifted stone is often cleansed before it is worn or used. This spell clears a secondhand piece with methods chosen to suit the material, since salt and water ruin some stones, then claims it with your own blessing. It works for estate jewelry, inherited pieces, vintage finds and crystals from any shop.

ingredients.item: Bowl of dry uncooked rice or dry sea salt (in a separate inner dish, not touching delicate stones)
White candle or white LED candle

steps: Check what the piece is made of. Pearl, opal, turquoise, malachite, selenite, amber, lapis lazuli and many soft or porous stones can be damaged by water or salt; clear quartz, amethyst and gold or silver settings are usually fine with dry methods.
Gently wipe the piece with the soft cloth to remove dust and the physical traces of its last owner.
Light the candle (or switch on the LED candle) and ring the bell or singing bowl three times over the piece, letting the sound wash through it.

For hardy pieces, nestle them into the bowl of dry rice or set them in a small dish placed on the dry salt so the salt does not touch delicate metals or stones; for delicate pieces, simply lay them on or beside the Selenite.
Hold your hands over the piece and speak the chant three times.
Leave the piece resting overnight, ideally where moonlight falls on it, then snuff the candle before you leave the room or go to bed.
In the morning, hold the piece, state what you want it to bring you, and wear or use it.
howToUse: Wear or use the piece right away to bond it to you. Repeat the bell and selenite cleansing any time it feels heavy, or monthly at the full moon. Throw the rice or salt in the trash; do not cook or eat it.
chant:
Other hands have held you long,
now their stories move along.
Cleared by sound and moon and stone,
from this day you are my own.
intention: I clear this piece of its past and claim it as a blessing for me.
timing: Monday (the Moon's day) or any full moon night.
bestTime: Any time; especially before first wearing an inherited or thrifted piece.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Water and salt can permanently dull, crack or dissolve soft and porous stones, pearls and some metals, so check the material first and use sound, moonlight or selenite for anything delicate. Selenite dissolves in water, so keep it dry. Some minerals, such as malachite, contain toxic elements; wash hands after handling raw stones and never put them in drinking water. Keep small jewelry and stones away from young children, as they are choking hazards. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk; do not eat the rice or salt.
pets: Keep small stones, rings and earrings away from pets, as they can be swallowed and cause blockages; keep loose salt out of reach.

name: Gentle Ward for a Child's Bedroom
description: Charms to protect sleeping children appear in folk practice the world over, from blessings said over cradles to protective symbols hung above the bed. This ward is designed for a child's room: no flames, no smoke, no essential oils in the air, and nothing small left within reach. A parent (or the child, if old enough) draws a protective picture, fills a sealed sachet of gentle chamomile and lavender, and blesses the room with a few kind words.

ingredients.item: Small fabric sachet, sewn or tied tightly closed

ingredients.amount: 1 large palm stone (bigger than a child's mouth) or skip it

steps: Tidy the room and open the window for a few minutes to let in fresh air.
Together with the child, draw a protective picture: a shield, a guardian animal, a sun or a star, and write the child's name on it.
Fill the sachet with the Chamomile and Lavender and sew or knot it tightly closed so nothing can spill out.
Switch on the LED candle or nightlight, and lightly mist the air (not the bed or the child) with the plain water, walking clockwise around the room.
Hold the picture and sachet and say the chant together.
Tape the picture above the door or bed, and place the sachet and Rose Quartz on a high shelf or tuck the sachet inside the pillowcase of an older child who will not chew it.
howToUse: Leave the picture up as long as the child likes it. Replace the herbs in the sachet every three months, composting the old ones. Say the chant together at bedtime whenever the child feels scared or after a bad dream.
chant:
Sun by day and stars by night,
keep this little one in light.
Gentle guard and gentle sleep,
safe and sound this room will keep.
intention: I surround this child and this room with gentle, loving protection.
timing: Monday (the Moon's day) in the evening before bedtime.
bestTime: Any time; especially when a child moves into a new room or is having bad dreams.
caution: This ward is flame-free and smoke-free; use only an LED candle or nightlight. Do not diffuse or spray essential oils in a child's room, as young children are more sensitive to them. Keep the sachet sewn shut and the stone on a high shelf away from babies and toddlers, since herbs and small objects are choking hazards; leave nothing in a baby's crib, as cribs should be kept bare for safe sleep. Check for plant allergies before using herbs near a child. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Chamomile and Lavender are listed by the ASPCA as toxic to dogs and cats if eaten; keep the sachet where pets cannot chew it.

name: Clearing the Air After an Argument
description: Even after people have made up, a room can feel thick and tense after a fight. In many folk practices, opening windows, clapping and ringing bells in corners is used to break up stagnant energy, and salt water is set out to absorb what remains. This spell clears the room itself so that heavy feelings do not linger; it pairs well with Mending a Quarrel when the relationship also needs healing.

ingredients.item: Small bell, or your own hands for clapping
Small bowl of water with a pinch of sea salt

steps: Wait until everyone has calmed down, then open the windows and doors of the room for at least ten minutes.
Starting at the doorway, walk counterclockwise around the room and clap sharply or ring the bell in each corner, where stuck energy is said to collect.
Twist the strips of Lemon peel to release their bright scent and drop them into the bowl of salt water.
Set the bowl and Rose Quartz in the center of the room and light the candle in a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish beside them.
Take three slow, deep breaths and speak the chant, letting your shoulders drop.
Close the windows, sit with the candle for a few quiet minutes, then snuff it out.
howToUse: Leave the bowl overnight, then pour it down the drain with running water and put the peel in the compost. Keep the Rose Quartz in the room as a reminder of peace. Repeat whenever a room feels heavy after conflict.
chant:
Angry words and heated air,
leave this room and leave us there.
Bell and salt and open door,
peace returns to us once more.
intention: I clear the heaviness of this argument from our space and welcome peace back in.
timing: As soon as possible after the argument; Friday (Venus) for harmony.
bestTime: Any time of year.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Lemon oil from the peel on your fingers can cause a skin rash in sunlight, so wash your hands after handling it. Keep the salt water bowl out of reach of small children. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk; do not drink the salt water. If an argument involved violence or threats, put your safety first and reach out for help.
pets: Lemons are listed by the ASPCA as toxic to dogs and cats, and salt water can cause salt poisoning; keep the bowl where pets cannot drink from it.

name: Horseshoe and Iron Nail Doorway Ward
description: Iron has been used as protection against ill-wishing and unfriendly spirits in British, Irish and wider European folklore for centuries, and a horseshoe nailed over the door is one of the best-known lucky charms in the English-speaking world. Customs differ on how to hang it: many hold that points up keeps luck from spilling out, while others hang it points down to pour protection over everyone who passes. This ward combines a horseshoe with four iron nails laid at the threshold to guard the doorway.
steps: Put on the work gloves. Wash the horseshoe and nails in the salt water, then dry them well so they do not rust further.
Hold the horseshoe and the Rosemary sprig together and speak the chant three times, asking the iron to guard your door.
Decide which way you will hang it (points up to hold luck, points down to pour protection), and mark the spot above the inside or outside of your front door.
Hammer two nails securely into the frame or wall and hang the horseshoe, checking that it cannot fall.
Place the four remaining nails at the four corners of the doormat, or tuck them under the mat or along the threshold, points facing outward.
Touch the horseshoe as you leave and say, 'Iron guard this door.'
howToUse: Leave the horseshoe up permanently; traditionally it is touched for luck on the way out. Check the nails under the mat each season, and replace any that have gone missing. Tuck the Rosemary sprig behind the horseshoe and replace it when it crumbles.
chant:
Iron shoe and iron nail,
guard this door and never fail.
Luck stay in and harm stay out,
iron strong, without a doubt.
intention: I guard my doorway with iron so that only good may enter and luck stays within.
timing: Saturday (Saturn, protection) or Tuesday (Mars, iron), during a waxing moon to draw luck.
bestTime: Any season; ideal when moving into a new home.
caution: Wear work gloves when handling rusty iron and keep your tetanus shots up to date, as puncture wounds from nails can cause tetanus; see a doctor if one breaks your skin. Hang the horseshoe securely with nails driven into a stud or solid frame so it cannot fall on anyone, and check before hammering that you are not over wiring or pipes. Place threshold nails flat, under the mat, where they cannot be stepped on with bare feet or pose a trip hazard, and keep them away from young children. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep loose nails and salt away from pets; nails can be swallowed or stepped on, and salt can cause salt poisoning.

name: Simmer Pot to Break a Run of Bad Luck
description: When misfortunes pile up one after another, some practitioners turn to the stove rather than the altar. A simmer pot of orange peel, bay, cinnamon and allspice fills the house with warm, lucky scent; in modern kitchen witchcraft, orange and cinnamon are associated with luck and success and bay with protection. Stirring counterclockwise breaks the streak, and stirring clockwise draws new luck in.
steps: On the paper, write 'My run of bad luck is broken,' and set it beside the stove, well away from the burner.
Fill the saucepan with the water and bring it to a gentle simmer on low heat.
Add the Bay Laurel leaves one at a time, naming a piece of bad luck you are breaking with each.
Stir counterclockwise nine times while saying, 'Bad luck, broken.'
Add the Orange Peel, Cinnamon sticks and Allspice, then stir clockwise nine times while speaking the chant.
Let it simmer on the lowest heat for up to two hours while you stay home and nearby, topping up with water so the pot never boils dry.
Turn off the stove when you are done, and tear the paper into small pieces and recycle or throw it away.
howToUse: Let the pot cool, then pour the liquid down the drain and compost the solids. Repeat for three days in a row for a stubborn run of bad luck, using fresh ingredients each time. Afterward, carry a bay leaf in your wallet as a reminder that the streak is broken.
chant:
Stir it out and stir it in,
bad luck ends and good begins.
Orange bright and bay leaf green,
the luckiest days I've ever seen.
intention: I break this run of bad luck and turn the tide toward good fortune.
timing: Thursday (Jupiter, luck) or Sunday; start on a waning moon and repeat into the new moon.
bestTime: Autumn and winter, when a warm simmer pot is most welcome.
caution: Never leave a pot on the stove unattended, and never let it boil dry, which can scorch the pan and start a fire. Keep the paper, towels and pot holders away from the burner, turn the pot handle inward, and keep children and pets away from the hot stove. The liquid is not a drink: do not drink the simmer pot, as it has been heated for hours and the whole bay leaves are a choking hazard. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Bay Laurel is listed by the ASPCA as toxic to dogs and cats, and large amounts of cinnamon or allspice can upset pets' stomachs; dispose of the used solids where pets cannot get them.

name: Apple Star Love-Drawing Candle
description: Apples have been tied to love in European folklore for centuries, from apple-peel divination to the old custom of sharing an apple with a sweetheart, and an apple cut crosswise reveals a five-pointed star of seeds at its heart. This candle spell surrounds a pink candle with that apple star, Rose and Lavender to call in a new love in general. It names the qualities you want in a partner rather than any particular person, so it draws a good match without touching anyone's free will.

ingredients.item: Apple, cut crosswise to show the seed star

steps: Set the pink candle firmly in its holder in the center of the heatproof plate.
On the paper, list the qualities you want in a partner and in a relationship, such as kindness, humor and honesty. Do not write anyone's name.
Fold the paper toward you three times and lay it on the plate, at least 3 inches from the candle.
Place the apple slice on top of the paper so the seed star faces up, and set the Rose Quartz beside it.
Make a ring of Rose petals, Lavender and a pinch of Cinnamon around the outer edge of the plate, keeping every bit of herb at least 3 inches from the flame.
Light the candle and read your list aloud, then speak the chant three times.
Sit with the candle for at least 15 minutes, imagining how it feels to be loved well, then snuff it out.
howToUse: Relight the candle for 15 minutes each evening until it is used up, repeating the chant. Replace the apple slice when it browns, composting the old one. When the candle is finished, carry the Rose Quartz with you, keep the folded list in your bedside drawer, and scatter the petals outdoors. Say yes to invitations and new places, since the spell opens doors that you still need to walk through.
chant:
Star of apple, heart of rose,
open the door that kindness knows.
A love that's free and true and kind,
come to me in heart and mind.
intention: I open my heart to a kind, honest love that chooses me freely.
timing: Friday (Venus) during the waxing moon, in the evening.
bestTime: Spring or early autumn apple season; any time you feel ready for love.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep dried petals, herbs and the paper at least 3 inches from the flame, since dried plant material catches fire easily; never sprinkle herbs onto the candle itself. Ground Cinnamon can irritate the eyes and skin, so wash your hands after handling it. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the plate out of reach; Lavender and Cinnamon can upset a pet's stomach, and apple seeds contain compounds harmful to pets if chewed.

name: Twin Flame Passion Rekindling
description: Paired red candles are a common modern folk-magic symbol for two partners and the warmth between them. This ritual is done by both partners together, with both agreeing to it, to rekindle passion and closeness in an existing relationship. It joins two flames into one, adds a gently scented massage oil, and asks each partner to say aloud what they love about the other.

ingredients.item: Sweet Almond Oil (or Jojoba Oil for nut allergies)
Small glass bottle or dish for the oil

steps: Agree together on the ritual and what you each hope to rekindle; this spell only works with both partners willing.
Set the two red candles side by side on the heatproof tray, about 6 inches apart, and scatter the Rose petals around the edge of the tray, well away from the flames.
Mix the Ylang Ylang and Sweet Orange Essential Oils into the Sweet Almond Oil in the bottle (about a 1% dilution) and swirl.
Each partner lights one candle while saying one thing they love and desire about the other.
Over the next few minutes, slide the candles closer together until they nearly touch, each partner holding their Carnelian or Garnet.
Speak the chant together, then exchange stones as a promise of renewed attention.
Snuff the candles together and use the oil for a slow shoulder or back massage, taking turns.
howToUse: Relight the candles together for a short time on the next few date nights, moving them closer each time, until they are used up. Keep the exchanged stones on your bedside table. Use the massage oil within a month and store it capped and away from heat. Pair the spell with real-world effort: scheduled time together, honest talk and touch.
chant:
Two flames rise and lean as one,
what we kindled is not done.
Warmth return and passion stay,
heart to heart, we find our way.
intention: We willingly rekindle our passion and closeness with each other.
timing: Friday or Tuesday evening during the waxing or full moon.
bestTime: Beltane (May 1), Valentine's season, or an anniversary.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep petals, hair, sleeves and bedding well clear of the flames, and snuff candles before moving to the bed. Never apply essential oils undiluted; keep the blend at about 1% in a carrier oil, patch test on the inner arm 24 hours first, and keep it away from eyes, genitals and other mucous membranes. Ylang Ylang can cause skin sensitization in some people. Oils can weaken latex condoms, so do not use the blend with them. Skip Sweet Almond Oil if either partner has a nut allergy and use Jojoba Oil instead. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the oil blend and candles out of reach; essential oils are harmful to cats and dogs if licked or absorbed, so do not let pets lick oiled skin.

name: Handfasting Ribbon Blessing
description: Handfasting was an old term in Scotland and northern England for a betrothal or marriage made by joining hands, and modern Wiccans and Pagans revived it as a wedding or commitment rite in which the couple's hands are bound with cord. This blessing braids three ribbons with Rosemary, long carried at English weddings for remembrance and faithfulness, to bless a handfasting, wedding vow renewal or anniversary. The braid becomes a keepsake of the promises made.

ingredients.item: Satin ribbons, about 1 yard each, in three colors of your choosing (for example white, red and green)
White pillar candle (for the shared flame)

steps: Each partner writes a short vow or anniversary promise on their own sheet of paper.
Set the three candles on the heatproof tray with the pillar in the middle, and lay the Rose petals in a heart shape on the table away from the flames.
Each partner lights one white candle while reading their vow aloud.
Together, use your two flames to light the central pillar, saying 'Two lights, one hearth.'
Knot the three ribbons together at one end; one partner holds the knot while the other braids, tucking a Rosemary sprig into the braid at the start, middle and end.
Loosely wrap the braid around your joined right hands and speak the chant together, then slip your hands free so the braid keeps its loop.
Tie off the end, fold the vows into the loop, and snuff the candles.
howToUse: Keep the braided ribbon and vows in a keepsake box or hang the braid near your bed. The Rosemary will dry in place. On each anniversary, take it out, reread the vows, and relight the pillar for a few minutes together. If you held a public handfasting, a friend or officiant can wrap the hands while the couple speaks the chant.
chant:
Three strands woven, two hands bound,
in this circle love is found.
Year by year and hand in hand,
by our promise, here we stand.
intention: We bless our union and renew the promises we freely make to each other.
timing: On your wedding or anniversary day; Friday or Sunday; full moon is ideal.
bestTime: Beltane (May 1) and Midsummer are traditional, but any anniversary works.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep ribbons, flowers, veils, sleeves and hair well clear of the flames, especially outdoors where wind can blow fabric into a candle; use glass hurricane shades outside. Never wrap the ribbons tightly enough to restrict circulation, and slip them off after a minute or two. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep ribbons out of reach of cats and dogs, since swallowed ribbon or string can cause a dangerous intestinal blockage.

name: Mended Heart Seed Pot
description: Planting seeds to mark a new chapter is a widespread folk custom, and the idea of letting the old compost into something new runs through many seasonal traditions. This spell for healing after a breakup turns the lessons of a past relationship into soil for something growing, with Calendula, long linked to comfort and the sun, as the seed. It honors what was good, releases what hurt, and gives you a daily, living sign of your own recovery.

ingredients.item: Small flower pot with a drainage hole and saucer

steps: On the paper, write in pencil what the relationship taught you and what you are ready to let go of. You may write their initials, but this spell is for your own heart, not for them.
Read it aloud once, then tear the paper into small pieces.
Fill the pot halfway with soil and scatter the torn paper and the Lavender over it.
Cover with more soil, leaving about half an inch at the top.
Press the seeds in about a quarter inch deep, naming one thing you want to grow in your own life for each seed.
Water gently while speaking the chant, and set the Rose Quartz on the soil.
Place the pot in a sunny window.
howToUse: Water the pot when the soil is dry to the touch and say the chant whenever you do. As the seedlings rise, notice how you are healing too. When they are strong, move them outdoors or into a bigger pot, and keep the Rose Quartz near your bed. If the seeds do not sprout, simply plant again; healing is not a test.
chant:
What we were I lay to rest,
I keep the lessons, leave the rest.
From broken ground new green will start;
seed by seed, I mend my heart.
intention: I release what has ended and grow a new, whole life for myself.
timing: Waning moon to release, or the new moon to begin again; Sunday or Monday.
bestTime: Spring is ideal for sprouting; indoors any time of year.
caution: Wear gloves when handling potting soil or wash your hands well afterward, and avoid breathing in dust from dry potting mix. Calendula is in the daisy family and may cause skin reactions in people allergic to ragweed, marigolds or daisies. If grief after a breakup feels overwhelming or lasts for weeks, please reach out to a friend, counselor or doctor; this spell is a companion to support, not a replacement for it. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the pot where pets cannot dig or chew; Lavender can upset a pet's stomach, and some potting mixes contain fertilizers that are harmful if eaten.

name: Rose and Oat Self-Love Bath
description: Ritual baths are found in many folk traditions, from cleansing baths in hoodoo to herbal baths in European cunning-folk practice, and Rose has long been a flower of love and tenderness. This gentle bath uses Rose, soothing Oat and Lavender to wrap you in care, turning ordinary bath time into a ritual of kindness to yourself. It is about softness and rest rather than fixing anything.

ingredients.item: Muslin bag, cotton sock or tea towel tied with string
Sweet Almond Oil (or Jojoba Oil for nut allergies)

steps: Tidy the bathroom and set the pink candle in a sturdy holder on a stable surface away from towels and curtains.
Fill the muslin bag with the Oats and Rose petals and tie it closed so nothing clogs the drain.
Mix the Lavender Essential Oil into the Sweet Almond Oil; essential oils do not dissolve in water, so always disperse them in a carrier first.
Run a warm (not hot) bath, hang the bag under the tap so water flows through it, then drop it in with the Epsom salt.
Swirl in the oil blend just before you step in, and place the Rose Quartz on the edge of the tub.
Light the candle, settle into the water, and speak the chant slowly.
Soak for 15 to 20 minutes, squeezing the bag over your shoulders and naming three things you like about yourself.
howToUse: Step out carefully, pat yourself dry and wrap up in something soft. Snuff the candle. Empty the bag's oats and petals into the compost or trash, not the drain. Keep the Rose Quartz by your bed. Repeat once a week, or whenever you need tenderness.
chant:
Petal soft and water warm,
I hold myself through every storm.
The love I give, I give to me;
as I will it, so mote it be.
intention: I treat myself with the same tenderness I would give someone I love.
timing: Friday evening (Venus); any moon, especially waxing or full.
bestTime: Any season; especially welcome in the colder months.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Never leave a candle burning in the bathroom while you are out of the room, and keep it away from towels, robes and shower curtains. Oil makes the tub very slippery, so step in and out slowly and use a bath mat; clean the tub afterward. Never add essential oils straight to bath water; keep them dispersed in a carrier oil at about 1-2%, and patch test first if you have sensitive skin. Keep the water warm rather than hot, and skip the bath if you are pregnant and unsure, have open wounds, or feel faint. Skip Sweet Almond Oil with a nut allergy. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep pets out of the bathroom during the ritual; essential oil residue in the tub can be harmful to cats and dogs if they lick it, so rinse the tub well.

name: New Baby Welcome Home Blessing
description: Blessing a household when a new baby arrives is found across countless cultures, from christening and naming customs to protective charms hung over the door. This gentle home blessing welcomes a newborn by blessing the front door and the family, not the baby's crib or body. It uses no flame, no smoke and no oils, and keeps every charm high out of the baby's reach.

ingredients.item: Small cloth sachet or pouch, tightly sewn or tied

steps: Before the baby comes home, or while someone else holds the baby in another room, stir the pinch of salt into the bowl of water.
Dip the Rosemary sprig and lightly flick drops of water on the outside of the front door and its frame, saying 'Only love may enter here.' Do not sprinkle water in the nursery or on baby items.
Fill the sachet with the Lavender, Chamomile and Rose petals, then tie or stitch it firmly closed.
Hang the sachet high on the outside of the front door or on a hall hook well above any child's reach.
On the card, write a short blessing for the baby, such as the qualities and joys you wish for them.
Gather the family together, read the blessing aloud and speak the chant.
Tuck the card into the baby book or a keepsake box.
howToUse: Leave the sachet on the door for a year and a day, then scatter its herbs outdoors and make a fresh one for the first birthday if you like. Pour the remaining salt water down the drain. Read the blessing card aloud again on the baby's birthdays.
chant:
Little one, the door is wide,
love and safety wait inside.
Blessed the threshold, blessed the hall,
blessed the home that holds us all.
intention: I bless our home and family as we welcome our new baby with love and safety.
timing: Any day the family is together; Monday (Moon) or Sunday (Sun) are lovely.
bestTime: Before or soon after the baby comes home, in any season.
caution: This spell intentionally uses no candles, incense, smoke or essential oils, because smoke and strong scents are not safe around infants. Never place sachets, crystals, cords or any charm in or near a crib, bassinet, car seat or anywhere near the baby's face; small items are choking and suffocation hazards, and loose objects do not belong in an infant's sleep space. Hang the sachet high and out of reach of all children. Do not use honey in any form for babies under 12 months. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Hang the sachet out of reach of pets; Lavender and Chamomile can upset a cat's or dog's stomach if chewed.

name: Peaceful Table Family Dinner Charm
description: The shared table and hearth have been the heart of family blessings in many traditions, from grace before meals to herbs laid under tablecloths for peace. This charm places a Bay Laurel leaf beneath the cloth and a simple centerpiece of Lavender and Rosemary to invite calm conversation and goodwill to a family dinner. It works on the atmosphere of the gathering and asks nothing of anyone's will.

ingredients.item: Small vase or jar of water
Blue or white candle (or a battery candle)

steps: Before guests arrive, write the word 'peace' on each Bay Laurel leaf with the pen.
Lay the three leaves under the tablecloth or placemat at the center of the table, forming a triangle.
Arrange the Lavender and Rosemary in the small vase and place it over the leaves.
Set the Blue Lace Agate at the foot of the vase.
Place the candle in a sturdy holder at the center of the table, away from serving dishes and anyone's reach.
Hold your hands over the centerpiece and speak the chant quietly.
Light the candle when everyone sits down, and invite each person to share one good thing from their week.
howToUse: Snuff the candle when the meal ends. Leave the Bay Laurel leaves under the cloth for the whole visit, then burn them safely in a fireplace or compost them. Keep the herb vase on the table until it fades. Use the charm for holidays, difficult reunions or any regular family dinner.
chant:
Bay beneath and herbs above,
fill this table up with love.
Gentle words and open ear,
only peace is welcome here.
intention: I invite calm, kindness and good conversation to our family table.
timing: The day of the gathering; Monday or Friday; any moon.
bestTime: Holidays such as Thanksgiving, Yule and family reunions.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep the candle away from napkins, paper decorations, sleeves, hair and serving dishes, and keep it well back from small children who may reach across the table; a battery candle is a safe alternative. The herbs and Bay Laurel leaves are decorative only and must not be cooked with or eaten, since dried bay leaves are a choking hazard. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk; the meal itself is your own ordinary food.
pets: Keep the vase and leaves out of reach; Bay Laurel and Lavender are toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

name: Two Moons Long-Distance Love Candle
description: Candles lit at the same hour in two places are a simple, popular modern way to feel connected across distance, echoing the old custom of a lamp left in the window for someone far away. In this spell both partners, by agreement, light a matching candle at the same time while on a call, looking at the same sky. It strengthens the bond you already share, keeps communication warm, and brings comfort until you are together again.

ingredients.item: Pink or white candles, one for each partner
Rose Quartz (tumbled), one for each partner
A photo of the two of you
Phone or computer for a call

steps: Agree on a time with your partner, ideally when the moon is visible to you both, and start a call.
Each set up your candle on a heatproof plate with the photo propped nearby, at least 12 inches from the flame.
Each write a short note about what you miss and what you look forward to doing together.
Light your candles at the same moment and read your notes to each other.
Hold your Rose Quartz and look at the moon or sky together, if you can, while speaking the chant at the same time.
Sprinkle a few Rose petals around the base of the plate, away from the flame, and let the candles burn while you talk for a while.
Snuff the candles together before you hang up.
howToUse: Repeat the candle call on the same night each week or month until the candles are used up. Carry your Rose Quartz daily and hold it when you miss each other. Mail your notes to each other, or keep them to read together when you reunite. Scatter the petals outdoors when you finish.
chant:
Under one moon, though miles apart,
one flame burns in each true heart.
Across the distance, love will stay,
until we meet another day.
intention: We keep our love warm and close across every mile between us.
timing: Full moon nights, or any agreed night each week; Friday or Monday.
bestTime: Any time you are apart, especially before a reunion.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep phones, chargers, photos and paper well away from the flame, and do not fall asleep on the call with the candle still lit. Keep dried petals at least 3 inches from the flame. Both partners should agree to the ritual. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep candles and crystals out of reach of pets, and never leave a lit candle in a room with an unattended cat or dog.

name: Marriage Hedge of Protection Jar
description: Protective jars and bottles have a long history in British and American folk magic, and Rosemary and Bay Laurel have been planted at doorways and hung in homes for protection for centuries. This jar is made by a couple together to shield their marriage or partnership from outside meddling, gossip and interference. It forms a protective hedge around the relationship, sending nothing harmful to anyone and simply keeping unwanted influence out.

ingredients.item: Glass jar with a tight lid
A photo of the two of you, or both your names on paper

steps: Agree together to make the jar; this is a shared working for both partners.
Light the white candle on a heatproof dish nearby and state together what outside pressures you want kept away.
Roll the photo or paper with both names into a scroll, facing inward, and place it in the jar.
Add the Rose Quartz for your love and the Black Tourmaline to guard it.
Pour in the salt as a boundary, then add the Rosemary and the two Bay Laurel leaves, one from each partner.
Close the lid tightly, hold the jar between you with all four hands, and speak the chant together.
Drip a little candle wax around the lid to seal it, letting it cool before handling.
howToUse: Keep the jar in your bedroom or near the front door, somewhere private. Hold it together whenever you feel outside pressure or meddling, and repeat the chant. Refresh it once a year on your anniversary: compost the herbs, rinse and cleanse the stones, pour the salt down the drain with running water, and remake it. Pair it with honest boundaries in daily life, such as agreeing together on what you share with others.
chant:
Salt and stone and bay and green,
none may come our hearts between.
Hedge us round and keep us true;
what's ours is ours, me and you.
intention: We protect our marriage from outside meddling and keep our bond strong and private.
timing: Saturday for protection, during the waning moon; or Friday under a full moon.
bestTime: Any season; especially after a wedding, move or family conflict.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Let sealing wax cool completely before touching, and drip it over a heatproof dish. Salt can damage plants and some surfaces, so pour it down the drain with running water rather than onto soil. Keep the jar and stones out of reach of small children, as tumbled stones are a choking hazard. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the jar sealed and out of reach; salt and Bay Laurel are harmful to pets if eaten.

name: New Pet Welcome Blessing
description: Blessing animals has a long history, from rural blessings of livestock to the modern Blessing of the Animals held in many churches around the feast of St. Francis in early October. This welcome rite brings a new pet into the family by blessing its new collar, water bowl and place in the home with words and touch alone. Unlike a protective charm, it is a gentle introduction ceremony, and nothing is ever put on, in or near the animal that it could chew or swallow.

ingredients.item: Your pet's new collar, harness or ID tag
Your pet's water bowl, with fresh plain water

steps: Before your pet arrives, or while they rest in another room, switch on the battery candle on a shelf in the room where the pet will spend the most time.
Hold the new collar or tag in both hands, say your pet's name aloud three times, and ask that they always find their way home.
Hold your hands over the bowl of plain water and speak a short blessing for health and comfort; do not add anything to the water.
On the card, write your pet's name, the date they joined the family and a welcome wish for them.
Gather the household, read the card aloud, and speak the chant.
Place the Rose Quartz and card on a high shelf near the pet's bed, well out of reach.
Put on the collar, offer the water bowl and give your pet a few of their usual treats as a welcome.
howToUse: Keep the card and Rose Quartz on the shelf, and reread the welcome on your pet's 'gotcha day' each year. Change the water daily as usual, renewing the blessing in your mind as you do. Give your new pet time and patience to settle; quiet and routine are the best magic for a nervous animal.
chant:
Paw and whisker, wing or tail,
here is home that will not fail.
Named and loved, now one of us,
welcome, friend, to all of us.
intention: I welcome our new pet into the family with love, safety and patience.
timing: The day your pet comes home, or the first full moon after; any day.
bestTime: Any season; around early October for the traditional Blessing of the Animals.
caution: This spell uses a battery candle because open flames, incense, smoke and essential oil diffusers are unsafe around pets, especially cats and birds. Never add herbs, salt, oils or crystals to a pet's water or food, and keep the Rose Quartz and card on a high shelf, since small objects can be swallowed and cause a blockage. Check the collar fit: you should be able to slide two fingers under it. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk by people; the pet only receives their usual plain water and treats.
pets: Keep crystals and cards out of reach, never put anything in the water bowl, and avoid smoke, incense and essential oil diffusers around pets, especially cats and birds.

name: Shared Hearth Roommate Harmony Bowl
description: Many households have kept a shared hearth charm or offering to keep peace among everyone under one roof, and Basil and Lavender are both linked in folk magic with harmony in the home. This spell is made together by roommates when someone new moves in, with each person adding an ingredient and a wish for the shared space. It pairs a herbal harmony bowl for the common room with a short written house agreement, so the magic and the practical side support each other.
steps: Gather all roommates in the kitchen or living room; everyone should want to take part.
Light the candle in a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish and welcome the new roommate by name.
Each person adds one herb to the bowl in turn, saying aloud a wish for the household, such as 'quiet mornings' or 'shared laughter.'
Stir the herbs clockwise together and set the stone in the center.
On the paper, write a few simple house agreements everyone has chosen, such as dishes, guests and quiet hours, and have everyone sign.
Hold hands or each place a hand on the table around the bowl and speak the chant together.
Fold the agreement and tuck it under the bowl, then snuff the candle.
howToUse: Keep the bowl in a shared space, out of reach of pets, for three months. Give it a stir and repeat the chant at house meetings or after any tension. When it fades, scatter the herbs outdoors, cleanse the stone, and remake it together, revising the house agreement if needed.
chant:
Many hands and one shared door,
peace and kindness on this floor.
Room by room and heart to heart,
each of us will do our part.
intention: We welcome our new roommate and make this a peaceful, fair and friendly home for all.
timing: The first week the new roommate moves in; Sunday or Monday; waxing moon.
bestTime: Any season, especially at the start of a lease or school term.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep the dry herb bowl at least 12 inches from the candle, as dried herbs catch fire easily. Check that no roommate has allergies to Chamomile or the daisy family, or to any herb used. Keep the stone out of reach of small children. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the bowl out of reach of pets; Lavender, Chamomile, Basil and citrus peel can upset a cat's or dog's stomach.

name: Wallet Money Keeper Charm
description: Folk customs in many places hold that a purse or wallet should never be left completely empty, and some people keep a 'lucky' coin or bill tucked away that is never spent. In some modern witchcraft traditions a folded bill is dressed with money herbs and a green stone so the wallet both draws money in and helps you hold on to it. This flat little charm rides in your wallet and reminds you to spend with intention.

ingredients.item: Paper bill of any amount (a dollar is fine)
Green Aventurine tumbled chip (small and flat)
Small green fabric square or envelope that fits your wallet

steps: Clean out your wallet first: remove old receipts, expired cards and clutter, and straighten your bills so they all face the same way.
Light the green candle in a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish and hold the bill in its warm glow (not in the flame) while you think about money arriving and staying.
Write a short wish on the Bay Laurel leaf with a pen, such as 'more in than out'.
Lay the leaf in the center of the bill, sprinkle on the pinch of Cinnamon, and set the Green Aventurine chip on top.
Fold the bill toward you three times, saying the chant once with each fold to draw money inward.
Slip the folded bill into the green fabric square or envelope and tie it closed with the green thread in three knots.
Tuck the charm into a hidden pocket of your wallet and snuff the candle.
howToUse: Carry the charm in your wallet and do not spend the bill inside it. Each time you open your wallet, take a breath and ask whether the purchase serves you. Refresh the herbs on the next New Moon or whenever the leaf crumbles, putting the old herbs in the trash or compost and keeping the same bill if you like.
chant:
Fold by fold and coin by coin,
to this purse may money join.
What comes in will gladly stay,
and none of it be thrown away.
intention: I welcome money into my wallet and hold on to it with wisdom and care.
timing: Thursday (Jupiter) or Sunday; during the hour of sunrise.
bestTime: Any time of year; the first days of a new month are traditional for money work.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep the bill and herbs away from the flame while you work. Ground Cinnamon can irritate eyes and skin, so wash your hands after handling it and do not breathe in the powder. The stone chip is a choking hazard for small children; keep the finished charm out of their reach. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the charm, the small stone and the Bay Laurel leaf away from pets; bay can upset a pet's stomach and a swallowed chip can cause a blockage.

name: Busy Shop Customer-Drawing Jar
description: Shopkeepers have long kept good luck charms near the register, and in hoodoo and rootwork, 'drawing' work for customers is a well-known category, often using magnetic Lodestone and sweet or money herbs. This jar is a simple, respectful version for a storefront counter, a market stall, or the desk where you run an online store. It sits beside your work as a steady signal for new and returning customers to find you.

ingredients.item: Small glass jar with a lid
Business card, receipt or a printout of your shop name and web address

steps: Tidy your counter or desk and wipe it down, since a clean, welcoming space is the first step in drawing customers.
Write your shop name, and your web address if you sell online, on the back of the business card along with the words 'customers come, buy and return'.
Roll the card toward you and place it in the jar.
Add the Sugar for sweet dealings, the Basil and Allspice for trade and money, then the coins.
Set the Lodestone and the Pyrite on top, telling them their job is to pull in people who will love what you offer.
Close the lid, set the jar on a heatproof dish, and light the tea light beside the jar (not on the lid) while you say the chant.
Let the tea light burn while you are present and working, then place the jar near your register, front door, or computer.
howToUse: Keep the jar near where sales happen. On busy days, give it a quick shake and thank it. Light a fresh tea light beside it once a week while you are working, and keep it running alongside real-world effort like good photos, clear prices and friendly follow-up. Refresh the herbs every three months; put the old herbs and sugar in the trash, wash the stones and reuse them.
chant:
Sugar sweet and stone that draws,
bring good buyers through these doors.
Seen and found and glad to stay,
customers come every day.
intention: I draw happy customers who value my work and return again and again.
timing: Wednesday (Mercury, trade) or Thursday; during business hours.
bestTime: Before a launch, sale, holiday shopping season or market weekend.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Never set a tea light directly on the jar lid or near shop stock, paper bags, price tags or computer cables, and blow it out before you step away or close for the day. Lodestone, Pyrite, coins and allspice berries are choking hazards for small children, so keep the jar sealed and out of their reach. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Shop cats and pets should not get into the jar; sugar, spices, coins and stones can cause stomach upset or a blockage if swallowed.

name: Debt Release and Budget Ritual
description: Waning moon work for shrinking and releasing things is common in modern witchcraft, and writing a burden on paper and then tearing or dissolving it is a familiar folk method. This ritual pairs that symbolic release with the honest, practical work that actually reduces debt: writing down every balance, making a budget and a payment plan. It helps ease the shame and dread around money so you can face it clearly.

ingredients.item: A copy of your bank, credit card and loan statements

steps: Gather your statements and, on the first sheet of paper, write down every debt: who it is owed to, the balance, the interest rate and the minimum payment. Looking at the real numbers is part of the spell.
Light the black candle in a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish and hold the Smoky Quartz while you breathe out the fear and shame you carry about these debts.
Stir the Salt and Rosemary into the bowl of water.
On a small strip torn from the second sheet, write 'I release the weight of debt' and dip it into the salted water, pressing it until the ink runs and the paper softens.
Light the green candle from the black one and, on the rest of the second sheet, write your plan: a monthly budget, one debt to focus on first, and one spending change you will make this month.
Speak the chant over the plan, then snuff the black candle and let the green one burn a little longer while you put a reminder of your first payment in your calendar.
Pour the water down the drain with running water and put the soggy paper in the trash, saying 'gone from me'.
howToUse: Keep the plan where you will see it, with the Smoky Quartz on top. Each time you make a payment, touch the stone and say 'lighter still'. Repeat the release on each waning moon until the debt is paid. If debts feel unmanageable, reach out to a reputable nonprofit credit counselor and be wary of debt relief companies that charge fees up front or promise to make debt disappear.
chant:
Balance by balance, line by line,
I face these numbers; the plan is mine.
With every payment, a weight let go,
as waning moon, my debts grow low.
intention: I release the fear around my debts and pay them down with a clear, honest plan.
timing: Saturday (Saturn, discipline); waning moon.
bestTime: Any time; the end of a month or the end of the year is a natural time to review finances.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep your statements and papers well away from both flames. Do not burn the papers; this spell dissolves them in water instead. This ritual supports, and does not replace, real financial steps; check any debt relief offer carefully, as the FTC warns about companies that charge up-front fees or make big promises. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the salt water where pets cannot drink it, since salt can make dogs and cats very sick.

name: Promotion and Raise Candle
description: Candle dressing, rubbing a candle with oil and rolling it in herbs, is a central method in hoodoo and in modern candle magic, and 'Crown of Success' is a traditional hoodoo condition oil name for recognition and advancement. Bay Laurel has crowned victors since ancient Greece and Rome. This candle is lit before you ask for a raise or apply for a promotion, to help you be seen and valued for the work you already do.

ingredients.item: Gold, yellow or green candle (taper or small pillar)
Crown of Success Oil (or Sunflower Oil with a pinch of dried herbs), already diluted for skin
Bay Laurel leaves, dried and crumbled
Plate or tray lined with foil

steps: On the slip of paper, write the role or pay you are asking for in specific words, and below it list three real accomplishments that show you have earned it.
Wearing gloves or with clean hands, rub a few drops of the oil onto the candle from the middle up to the top and from the middle down to the bottom, thinking about rising.
Mix the crumbled Bay Laurel, Cinnamon and Calendula on the foil-lined plate and roll the oiled candle lightly in them, then brush off any loose bits so they do not catch fire.
Set the candle in a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish, with the paper under the dish (not under the flame) and the Citrine beside it.
Light the candle and read your accomplishments aloud, then speak the chant three times.
Let the candle burn while you prepare: update your resume, gather numbers about your results, and practice how you will make your request.
Snuff the candle when you finish and relight it for short sessions until it is burned down, never leaving it alone.
howToUse: Carry the Citrine or Tiger's Eye in your pocket to the meeting where you ask. Keep the paper in your work bag until you hear back. Once the candle has burned down, scrape any leftover wax and herbs into the trash. If the answer is not yet, ask what would earn a yes and repeat the spell when you have done it.
chant:
Laurel crown and golden flame,
let my worth be known by name.
What I've built, let others see;
raise and rise come now to me.
intention: I am recognized and fairly rewarded for the value I bring to my work.
timing: Sunday (Sun, recognition) or Thursday (Jupiter, growth); waxing moon.
bestTime: A few weeks before performance reviews, budget season or the end of a fiscal year.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Dressed candles burn hotter and can flare, so roll only a light coat of herbs, brush off loose bits, and never let herbs pile up around the wick. Use only oil that is already diluted for skin (about 1 to 2 percent, or 6 to 12 drops of essential oil per 30 ml of carrier oil); wash your hands afterward and stop if your skin reacts. Cinnamon oil and powder are especially irritating. Never swallow essential oils. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep pets away from the lit candle; essential oils and Cinnamon can be harmful to cats and dogs if licked or inhaled in concentrated amounts.

name: Interview Calm Voice Pocket Stone
description: Carrying a charged stone in the pocket as a touchstone for courage is a common practice in modern crystal and folk magic, and Rosemary has been tied to memory and a clear mind since at least the time of Shakespeare's Ophelia. Where a job-seeking charm draws offers in, this charm is for the interview itself: steady nerves, a clear voice, and remembering what you meant to say. You charge it while rehearsing your answers, so touching it in the room brings back that calm.

ingredients.item: Tiger's Eye or Carnelian, tumbled and pocket-size
Blue Lace Agate or Sodalite, tumbled (for clear speech)
Small cloth pouch or a clean handkerchief
List of likely interview questions and your notes

steps: The night before your interview, light the candle in a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish and sit with your list of questions.
Brush the Rosemary sprig gently over both stones, breathing in its scent and saying 'clear mind, steady heart'.
Hold the Tiger's Eye or Carnelian in your dominant hand and the Blue Lace Agate or Sodalite in the other, and answer each practice question aloud as if you were already in the room.
When you stumble, pause, squeeze the stones, take one slow breath, and begin the answer again. This teaches your body that the stones mean calm.
Finish by saying the chant three times, then wrap both stones and the Rosemary sprig in the pouch or handkerchief.
Snuff the candle and get a good night's sleep.
howToUse: On the day, carry the stones in your pocket or bag; for a video interview, keep them on the desk out of camera view. Before you walk in or log on, squeeze them once and take a slow breath. Afterward, compost the Rosemary, rinse the stones under running water, and keep them for your next interview, first day or difficult conversation.
chant:
Stone of courage, stone of voice,
steady me in every choice.
Clear my mind and calm my breath;
let me speak my very best.
intention: I walk into my interview calm, clear and confident, and I speak my strengths with ease.
timing: The night before the interview; Wednesday (Mercury, speech) if you have a choice.
bestTime: Any time of year, whenever an interview is scheduled.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Snuff the candle before you go to sleep. Tumbled stones are a choking hazard for young children, so keep them out of their reach. Rinse stones only briefly in water and do not make them into drinks. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the stones away from pets who chew, since a swallowed stone can cause a blockage.

name: Sold House Key and Simmer Spell
description: One well-known American folk custom for selling a house is burying a small statue of St. Joseph, a Catholic practice that people of that faith may prefer to follow in their own way. This spell takes a different, non-religious route: a house key charm is blessed to call in the right buyer, and a cinnamon and orange simmer pot fills the home with a warm, welcoming scent for showings. It also asks you to let go of the house emotionally so it can belong to someone new.
steps: Walk through each room and thank the house out loud for the years it sheltered you, naming a good memory in each space. Declutter and clean as you go, since a tidy home sells better.
Write 'SOLD to the right buyer, at a fair price' on the Bay Laurel leaf.
Thread the ribbon through the spare key, wrap the bay leaf around the key, and tie it with three knots, speaking the chant once for each knot.
Set the bundled key and the Citrine or Pyrite just inside the front door, on a shelf or in a drawer near the entry.
Before each showing or open house, put the Cinnamon sticks, Orange Peel and Clove in the pot with the water and bring it to a gentle simmer on the stove.
Stay in the kitchen while it simmers, add water as it gets low, and turn it off and take it off the heat before you leave the house for the showing.
howToUse: Leave the key charm by the door until the sale closes. On closing day, untie it, place the bay leaf in the compost or trash, and leave the clean key for the new owners or hand it over with the others. Make a fresh simmer pot for each showing; the cooled mixture can be poured out and composted. The simmer pot is for scent only, not for drinking.
chant:
Key and laurel, warm and sweet,
bring the buyer I'm meant to meet.
Fair the price and smooth the sale,
new hands to love it without fail.
intention: I release this house with gratitude and welcome the right buyer at a fair price.
timing: Thursday or Sunday; begin on a waxing moon, before the listing goes live.
bestTime: Spring and early summer are peak home-selling seasons, but work it whenever you list.
caution: Never leave a simmer pot on the stove unattended, and never leave it on when you go out for a showing; set a timer, keep water in the pot so it does not boil dry and scorch, and turn handles inward away from children. Keep towels, paper listings and oven mitts away from the burner. Whole Clove and Cinnamon can irritate skin and eyes, so wash your hands after handling them. The simmer pot is not a drink and nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep pets away from the hot stove and the simmering pot, and dispose of the spent spices where dogs cannot get into them, as spices can upset their stomachs.

name: Scholarship and Grant Application Blessing
description: Blessing important papers before sending them, such as touching them to an altar or anointing a corner, is a practice found in several folk traditions, including some hoodoo work for letters and applications. This spell blesses a scholarship, grant or fellowship application so it stands out to the people who read it. It works best paired with the practical magic of meeting deadlines, following instructions and proofreading.

ingredients.item: Printed copy of your application, essay or cover page

steps: Before you begin, proofread your application one last time and check every requirement on the funder's list. This is part of the spell.
Light the candle in a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish, a safe distance from your papers.
Write the name of the scholarship or grant on the Bay Laurel leaf and place it in the small dish with the Calendula petals.
Lay the printed application flat beside the dish, with the Citrine on top for success and the Fluorite or Clear Quartz on top for a clear, compelling message.
Read your opening sentence aloud, then speak the chant three times with one hand resting on the papers.
Submit the real application online or by mail while the candle is still burning, then snuff it.
howToUse: Keep the blessed printout, Bay Laurel leaf and stones together in a folder or on your desk until you hear back. When a decision arrives, thank the leaf and compost it with the Calendula. Reuse the stones for your next application, and send thank-you notes to anyone who wrote you a recommendation.
chant:
Laurel leaf and marigold,
let my story's worth be told.
Readers see the best in me;
funds and doors are opened free.
intention: My application is read with care and I receive the funding that helps me grow.
timing: Wednesday (Mercury) or Thursday (Jupiter); waxing moon, before the deadline.
bestTime: Late fall through spring, when most scholarship and grant deadlines fall.
