caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep your printed application, notes and dried herbs well away from the flame, and do not hold papers over the candle. People allergic to ragweed, daisies or marigolds may react to Calendula, so wash your hands after handling it. The stones are choking hazards for small children. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep stones and herbs out of reach of pets, and keep pets away from the lit candle.

name: Wise Counsel Sage and Rosemary Tea
description: Garden Sage takes its name from the Latin salvia, 'to save' or 'to heal', and both Sage and Rosemary have long been linked with wisdom and memory in European herbal lore. This gentle tea ritual uses culinary garden Sage (Salvia officinalis, not White Sage) and Rosemary in ordinary food amounts. Sip it slowly while you weigh a big decision, so you can listen to your own good sense.

ingredients.item: Sage, dried culinary garden sage (Salvia officinalis)

steps: If you like, light the candle in a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish and sit somewhere quiet with your journal.
At the top of a page, write the decision you are facing as one clear question.
Place the Sage and Rosemary in the strainer in your mug, pour the boiling water over them, and cover the mug for 5 minutes while the steam rises.
Remove the herbs, add the Lemon slice and Honey if you like, and hold the warm mug while you speak the chant.
Sip slowly. Below your question, write two columns: what each choice would bring, and how each choice feels in your body.
When the cup is finished, write one sentence that begins 'The wise choice for me is...' even if it is only 'to wait and gather more information'.
Snuff the candle and compost the used herbs.
howToUse: Sleep on your answer before acting on any major decision. Return to the journal page the next morning and see whether your answer still feels right. Keep this to one cup on a given day, and no more than a few times a week. Compost the spent herbs.
chant:
Sage of wisdom, Rosemary clear,
let the truest path appear.
Calm my mind and still my doubt;
let the wise choice now come out.
intention: I quiet my mind and listen to my own wisdom so I can make a good decision.
timing: Wednesday (Mercury) or Thursday; full moon for clarity or any quiet evening.
bestTime: Any time of year, whenever a decision needs a clear head; autumn suits reflection.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Use only culinary garden Sage and Rosemary from the spice aisle or garden, in the small amounts given; do not use White Sage, sage essential oil or rosemary essential oil in the tea, and never swallow essential oils. Sage contains thujone, which in large or long-term amounts can cause seizures and other harm, so keep to one cup and avoid the tea if you have epilepsy or a seizure disorder. Avoid medicinal amounts of Sage and Rosemary if pregnant or breastfeeding, and avoid this tea if you are allergic to plants in the mint family. Handle boiling water with care. Do not give honey to babies under 12 months. Edible part: the strained tea, with lemon and honey if used.
interactions: In food amounts, Sage and Rosemary are unlikely to cause problems, but larger amounts may interact with some medicines. Sage may affect blood sugar and may add to the effects of diabetes medicines and sedatives, and its thujone may lower the seizure threshold and interfere with anticonvulsant medicines. Rosemary may interact with blood thinners (anticoagulant and antiplatelet drugs), ACE inhibitors, diuretics and lithium. If you take any of these, or have a seizure disorder, check with your doctor or pharmacist before drinking herbal tea regularly.
pets: Do not share the tea with pets, and keep honey and the lemon away from them.

name: Lucky Lottery Ticket Blessing
description: Gamblers' luck charms are a lively part of American folk magic: hoodoo players have long carried things like a whole nutmeg or a 'lucky hand' and washed their hands in Chamomile before playing. This lighthearted blessing is a bit of fun for a single lottery or scratch ticket you buy for entertainment, not a plan for getting rich. It asks for luck, and it asks you to play only what you can comfortably afford to lose.

ingredients.item: Lottery or scratch ticket, bought within a budget you set ahead of time
Warm water in a small bowl

steps: Decide how much you are willing to spend on fun this month before you buy anything, and buy only within that amount.
Steep the Chamomile tea bag in the bowl of warm water for 5 minutes, then let it cool to a comfortable temperature.
Light the green candle in a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish.
Dip your fingertips in the Chamomile water, then dry your hands thoroughly so the ticket stays clean.
Place the ticket in the envelope with the pinch of Cinquefoil, which in some traditions is said to grasp luck with its five fingers, and set the Green Aventurine on top.
Say the chant once, with a smile, then snuff the candle and leave the envelope by the candle until the drawing or until you scratch the ticket.
howToUse: Check your ticket after the drawing, whatever happens, and say 'thank you for the fun'. If you win something, consider sharing a little of it as a gift or a donation. Pour the cooled Chamomile water down the drain or onto a plant, and put the Cinquefoil in the trash. If gambling stops feeling fun, or you find yourself chasing losses or spending more than you planned, call or text 1-800-GAMBLER for free, confidential help.
chant:
Five-finger grass and lucky green,
bring the best I've ever seen.
Win or lose, I play for fun;
laughter's mine when all is done.
intention: I play for fun within my budget and welcome a lucky surprise with a light heart.
timing: Thursday (Jupiter, luck) or the day of the drawing; any hour you feel lucky.
bestTime: Any time of year, for fun; birthdays and holidays are popular ticket days.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep the ticket and envelope away from the flame. People allergic to ragweed, daisies or chrysanthemums can react to Chamomile, even on the skin. This is a playful blessing, not a way to make money: only adults of legal age should play, never spend money meant for bills, and seek help through the national helpline at 1-800-GAMBLER if play feels out of control. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the stone and dried herbs away from pets, and keep pets away from the lit candle.

name: Scales of Fairness Justice Petition
description: Writing a petition, a short paper stating what you ask for, is a core practice in hoodoo and in many folk traditions, and the balanced scales have stood for justice since ancient Egypt and Greece. This petition does not ask for anyone to be punished or harmed. It asks only that the truth come out and that a dispute, such as a disagreement with a landlord, an insurance claim, a workplace complaint or a school appeal, be decided fairly for everyone.

ingredients.item: Two small matching dishes or saucers (for the scales)
Copies of your documents, emails or evidence

steps: Gather and organize your records: dates, emails, receipts and photos. Being prepared is the most powerful part of this petition.
Set the two small dishes side by side on your altar or table to represent the scales, and place the candle in a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish between them.
On the paper, write your petition in calm, fair words, for example: 'Let the truth be seen clearly, and let this matter be decided fairly for all involved.' Do not wish harm on anyone.
Place one Bay Laurel leaf and half the Calendula in each dish, so both sides begin equal.
Set the Lapis Lazuli on one dish and the Clear Quartz on the other, then light the candle and read your petition aloud.
Speak the chant three times, then fold the petition toward you and tuck it beneath the candle dish.
Let the candle burn while you write down your next practical step, such as filing a complaint, requesting mediation or calling a legal aid office, then snuff it.
howToUse: Relight the candle for short sessions while the matter is open, and keep the petition with your important papers. Bring the Lapis Lazuli with you to hearings, meetings or calls about the dispute. When it is resolved, whatever the outcome, thank the scales, compost the herbs, and tear the petition and put it in the trash. For legal matters, follow the advice of a qualified lawyer or legal aid service.
chant:
Even scales and steady light,
let the truth be brought to sight.
No harm I send, no ill I ask;
let fairness rule in this task.
intention: I ask that the truth be seen and that this matter be decided fairly for everyone involved.
timing: Thursday (Jupiter, justice) or Saturday (Saturn, law); waxing to full moon.
bestTime: Any time of year, when a dispute or decision is pending.
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep your documents, petition paper and dried herbs well away from the flame; tuck the petition under the dish, never under the candle itself. Lapis Lazuli and Sodalite should not be soaked in drinking water or made into elixirs. Those allergic to ragweed or marigolds may react to Calendula. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep pets away from the lit candle and keep stones and herbs where they cannot be chewed.

name: Money Plant Potting Spell
description: Round-leaved houseplants such as the Chinese money plant (Pilea peperomioides) and the jade plant are popular modern prosperity plants, partly through feng shui-inspired practice and partly because their coin-shaped leaves invite the idea. In this spell you pot or repot a money plant with a few coins and a green stone, so that as you care for it, your prosperity grows with it. The Chinese money plant is used here because it is considered safe for pets and children.

ingredients.item: Chinese money plant (Pilea peperomioides) in a nursery pot
Pot with a drainage hole, one size larger

steps: Put on your gloves and pour a layer of potting mix into the new pot.
Press the three coins into the soil in a triangle, saying 'one to arrive, one to stay, one to grow'.
Sprinkle the pinch of Basil over the coins and set the Green Aventurine or Pyrite in the center.
Ease the plant out of its nursery pot, loosen the roots gently with your fingers, and set it on top of the coins and stone.
Fill in around it with potting mix, firm it lightly, and water slowly until water runs from the drainage hole.
Hold your hands around the leaves and speak the chant three times.
Place the plant in bright, indirect light, near your front door, desk or in the far left corner of a room, which feng shui-inspired practice links with wealth.
howToUse: Water when the top inch of soil is dry and turn the pot a quarter turn each week so it grows evenly. Each time you water, name one thing you are doing to grow your finances. When the plant makes baby plantlets, pot them up and give them to friends to share the prosperity. If the plant ever dies, compost it, keep the coins, and start again with thanks.
chant:
Coin-round leaf and rooted stone,
grow my wealth as you have grown.
Water, light and patient care;
plenty here and plenty there.
intention: As I tend this plant, my prosperity takes root and grows steadily.
timing: Thursday (Jupiter) or Friday; waxing moon, during daylight.
bestTime: Spring or early summer, when houseplants are actively growing and easiest to repot.
caution: Wear gloves when handling potting mix, avoid breathing in its dust, and wash your hands afterward. Coins and small stones in the pot are choking hazards for young children, so keep the pot out of their reach. If you choose a jade plant instead of a Chinese money plant, know that it is toxic to cats and dogs. No candle is used in this spell. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: The Chinese money plant is considered pet-safe, but jade plants are toxic to cats and dogs (vomiting, depression, incoordination and, rarely, a slow heart rate), so choose the Pilea if you have pets, and keep pets from digging out the coins and stone.

name: Mabon Balance and Gratitude Spell
description: Mabon is the modern Pagan name for the autumn equinox, the second harvest, when day and night stand equal before the dark half of the year begins. The name was given to the festival in the 1970s, but giving thanks for the harvest at this time of year is far older. This spell uses a black and a white candle and a halved apple to weigh what you are grateful for against what you are ready to let go, bringing your life back into balance.

ingredients.item: Oak leaves or acorns, or a few fallen autumn leaves

steps: Set the white candle on the right and the black candle on the left of your altar or table, each in a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish, with the plate between them.
Lay the leaves or acorns around the plate as a small harvest wreath and light both candles, the light and the dark together.
Fold the paper in half. On the right side write the harvests you are thankful for this year; on the left write what feels heavy, unfinished or out of balance.
Cut the apple across its middle to reveal the five-pointed star of seeds, a sign of the turning year in many modern traditions.
Drizzle a little honey and a pinch of Cinnamon on both halves, then read your gratitude list aloud over the right half and your burdens over the left.
Speak the chant, then eat the right half slowly, taking in your blessings, and set the left half aside as an offering.
Sit quietly until you feel steady, then snuff both candles together.
howToUse: Take the left half of the apple outdoors and leave it beneath a tree or bury it in the garden, giving your burdens back to the earth to compost. Keep the gratitude side of the paper on your altar until Samhain and tear off and bury the burden side with the apple. Repeat the gratitude list whenever life feels lopsided over the autumn.
chant:
Light and dark in even scale,
the harvest in, the year grows pale.
What I've reaped I bless and keep,
what weighs on me, the earth may keep.
intention: I give thanks for all I have harvested and restore balance by releasing what weighs me down.
timing: Autumn equinox (around September 21-23) at sunset; Sunday or Saturday.
bestTime: Early autumn, Mabon / autumn equinox (Sep 21-23)
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep the dry leaves and paper well away from the flames. Check for allergies before sharing the apple, use care with the knife, and do not give honey to babies under 12 months. Apple seeds contain small amounts of compounds that release cyanide when crushed, so do not chew or swallow the seeds. Edible part: the apple half with honey and Cinnamon.
pets: Apple seeds, stems and leaves are toxic to dogs, cats and horses; leave only the flesh as an outdoor offering, or bury it, so pets and wildlife cannot eat the core.

name: Samhain Ancestor Remembrance Candle
description: Samhain, on the night of October 31, is the Gaelic festival that ends the harvest and, in folk belief, a time when the veil between the living and the dead grows thin. Lighting a candle in a window to guide the spirits of family home is a custom found in Ireland and in many other cultures around this time of year. Unlike a full Dumb Supper, this is a simple candle vigil: you dress a candle with Rosemary for remembrance, speak your ancestors' names, and keep their light for one night.

ingredients.item: White or orange pillar candle in a glass holder
Photos or written names of your ancestors and beloved dead
Apple or small pumpkin, as an offering

steps: Clean the window sill or table where the candle will stand and set the heatproof tray there, well away from curtains and blinds.
Rub a few drops of oil onto the sides of the candle, never the wick, from the top down, then roll it lightly in the crumbled Rosemary, brushing off any loose bits that could flare.
Arrange the photos or names around the tray, with the bowl of water and the apple or pumpkin as gifts for the visiting dead.
At dusk, light the candle and say, 'This light is for you,' then speak each ancestor's name aloud, slowly, with one memory of them if you have one.
Speak the chant three times and sit with the candle for a while, listening, remembering, or simply keeping them company.
Before you go to bed, thank your ancestors and snuff the candle; never leave it burning overnight.
howToUse: Relight the candle for short vigils over the three nights around Samhain, snuffing it each time you leave the room. Afterward, pour the water and leave the offering outside at the foot of a tree, or compost it. Keep the photos out until November 2 (All Souls' Day) if you wish, then put them away with thanks.
chant:
By rosemary for memory,
by flame upon the sill,
come home, my kin, and sit with me,
for you are honored still.
intention: I remember and honor my ancestors and beloved dead, and welcome their love and wisdom this Samhain night.
timing: Samhain night (October 31) at dusk; dark moon or waning moon.
bestTime: Mid-autumn, Samhain (Oct 31-Nov 2)
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. A window candle sits close to curtains and blinds, so tie them back or place the candle on a table nearby instead, and always snuff it before you leave the room or go to sleep; a flameless LED candle is a safe choice for a candle that stays in the window all night. Oil and loose herbs on a candle can make it flare, so dress it lightly, keep oil off the wick and brush away loose Rosemary. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep pets away from the lit candle and offerings; remove the offering before it spoils.

name: Yule Sun-Return Orange Pomander
description: Clove-studded oranges were a popular Christmas and winter gift in Britain and Europe by the Victorian era, and sweet-smelling pomanders were carried for centuries before that. For modern witches, the round golden orange stands for the reborn sun at Yule, the winter solstice, and the cloves for warmth, protection and prosperity. Making a pomander turns slow, patient handwork into a charm that welcomes the returning light into your home.

ingredients.item: Thimble or cloth tape for your fingertip

steps: Wash and dry the orange, then wrap the ribbon around it in a cross, like a parcel, to mark four quarters for the four seasons, and pin the ends with a clove or two.
Using the toothpick, pierce small holes in the peel within each quarter, in lines, spirals or sun shapes.
Push a whole Clove into each hole, wearing the thimble, and with each one name a blessing you wish for the coming year.
Fill the quarters closely with cloves; the more you cover the peel, the better the orange will dry.
Mix the Cinnamon and Allspice in the paper bag, drop in the orange, and shake gently to coat it, then speak the chant over it.
Leave the orange in the bag or on a wire rack in a cool, dry, airy spot for two to four weeks, turning it daily, until it is light and hard.
Tie a loop in the ribbon and hang the pomander in your home on the solstice.
howToUse: Hang the pomander in a doorway, closet or near the hearth from Yule through the winter as a charm of warmth, light and protection. Squeeze it gently now and then to release its scent. A well-dried pomander can last a year; if it ever grows mold or softens, thank it and compost it, and make a fresh one next Yule.
chant:
Golden sun in winter's hold,
studded bright with clove and gold,
the longest night is turned at last;
return, O light, the dark is passed.
intention: I welcome the return of the sun and fill my home with warmth, light and blessings for the year ahead.
timing: Begin at the start of December so it is dry by Yule; Sunday for sun magic.
bestTime: Winter, Yule / winter solstice (Dec 20-23)
caution: Clove contains eugenol, which can irritate skin and sensitive fingertips, and ground Cinnamon can irritate skin and eyes, so protect your finger with a thimble or tape, avoid touching your eyes, and wash your hands well afterward. Keep the skewer and loose cloves away from small children, who could choke on them. Check the pomander for mold while it dries and discard it if mold appears, especially in a home with anyone who has asthma or mold allergies. The pomander is a decoration only: nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Citrus peel and oils, cloves and essential oil compounds can upset dogs and cats; hang the pomander out of reach and pick up any dropped cloves.

name: Dark Moon Shadow-Work Journaling Ritual
description: Shadow work, a term borrowed from Carl Jung's idea of the 'shadow' self, is the practice of gently looking at the parts of ourselves we hide, deny or judge. Many modern witches set this inner work at the dark moon, the quiet night or two when the moon cannot be seen and is linked with rest, endings and hidden things. This ritual pairs a black candle and a grounding stone with guided journal prompts so you can meet your shadow with curiosity and kindness rather than fear.

ingredients.item: Smoky Quartz or Obsidian tumbled stone

steps: Choose a quiet evening when you have an hour alone and feel steady enough for reflection; if you are in crisis, set this aside and reach out for support instead.
Brew the Chamomile tea if using, wrap up in the blanket, and set the bowl of salt beside you as a reminder that you can always ground and come back.
Light the black candle in its holder on a heatproof dish and hold the Smoky Quartz or Obsidian in your nondominant hand.

Speak the chant, then write freely in response to one or two prompts: 'What do I criticize most in others, and where does it live in me?', 'What feeling do I avoid at all costs?', 'What did I learn to hide as a child, and why?'
Write without editing or judging for at least ten minutes, then read back what you wrote and underline one thing you can treat with more compassion.
Close with a kind word to yourself, such as 'This too is part of me, and I am safe.'
Press your hands into the salt to ground, then snuff the candle and close the journal.
howToUse: Keep the journal private and return to it each dark moon, noticing patterns over the months. Carry the stone when old feelings come up during the month. Sprinkle the used salt outdoors on bare ground or rinse it down the drain. If the work stirs up feelings that are hard to carry, talk to a trusted friend, therapist or counselor.
chant:
Moon unseen and night so deep,
show me what I hide and keep.
What I meet, I hold with grace;
my shadow, too, may have its place.
intention: I meet my hidden self with honesty and compassion, and grow whole by understanding it.
timing: Dark moon, evening; Saturday or Monday.
bestTime: Any time of year; especially late autumn and winter
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Keep the journal pages and blanket well back from the flame. This spell supports, and never replaces, medical or mental health care. Shadow work can bring up painful memories; stop and ground whenever you feel overwhelmed, and if you have thoughts of harming yourself, call or text 988 in the US (or your local emergency number) right away. Chamomile can cause allergic reactions in people sensitive to ragweed, daisies or related plants. Edible part: the Chamomile tea (optional).
interactions: Chamomile tea may add to the effects of sedatives and may interact with blood thinners such as warfarin; ask your doctor or pharmacist if you take these, and avoid it if pregnant unless your provider says it is fine.
pets: Keep the candle away from pets; Chamomile is listed by the ASPCA as toxic to dogs, cats and horses, so do not leave the tea or flowers where they can reach them.

name: Lunar Eclipse Release Spell
description: A lunar eclipse happens when the Earth passes between the sun and a full moon, and the moon darkens, often to a coppery red, as it moves through Earth's shadow. In many cultures eclipses were seen as powerful or unsettling turning points, and modern witches often treat them as a once-in-a-while chance for deep release and fast change. In this spell you write what you are done with on dissolving paper and let the eclipsed moon carry it away in a bowl of salt water.

ingredients.item: Dissolving paper, rice paper or a square of toilet paper

steps: Look up the exact time of totality for your area, and find a safe spot outdoors or at a window where you can see the moon.
Stir the salt into the bowl of water and drop the Moonstone in, asking it to hold the moon's power for you. Set the Selenite beside the bowl, not in the water.
As the Earth's shadow begins to cover the moon, write on the paper the habit, fear, pattern or tie you are ready to release, in a few simple words.
At or near totality, when the moon is darkest or reddest, hold the paper over the bowl and speak the chant.
Lay the paper on the water and swirl it gently counterclockwise, the direction of release,, watching it soften and fall apart as you breathe out slowly.
Watch as the moon's light returns, and hold the Selenite as a sign that clear light follows every shadow.
Take the Moonstone out of the water, dry it, and keep it by your bed.
howToUse: Pour the water and dissolved paper onto bare ground away from plants, or down the drain with running water. Keep the Moonstone as a reminder of your release and hold it whenever the old pattern tries to return. Expect change to come quickly after an eclipse, and support it with practical steps over the next six months, until the next eclipse season.
chant:
Shadow over silver face,
take what's done from time and place.
As the red moon fades to white,
so I'm freed into the light.
intention: I release what no longer serves me, and as the moon's light returns, I step forward free.
timing: During a total or partial lunar eclipse, ideally at totality.
bestTime: Eclipse season, whenever a lunar eclipse is visible from your area
caution: A lunar eclipse is safe to look at with your naked eyes, but a solar eclipse is not, so never use this spell as a reason to look at the sun. Eclipse nights can be cold and dark: dress warmly, watch your footing, and stay in a safe, well-known place. Do not put Selenite in water, as it is soft and slowly dissolves; keep it dry. Salt water kills plants, so do not pour it on gardens or lawns. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Do not leave the salt water where pets can drink it; salt can cause vomiting, tremors and seizures in dogs and cats.

name: Moonlit Scrying Bowl
description: Scrying, gazing into a reflective surface to receive images or impressions, is one of the oldest forms of divination, and water in a dark bowl has been used for it in many parts of the world. In European folk practice, moonlight on still water was thought to make visions clearer. This spell prepares a dark scrying bowl with a pinch of Mugwort and a Moonstone so you can quiet your mind and look for the symbols that rise.

ingredients.item: Dark or black bowl, wide and shallow

ingredients.amount: enough to nearly fill the bowl

steps: On a clear night near the full moon, set the bowl where moonlight can fall on it, by a window or outdoors on a steady table.
Place the Moonstone or Amethyst in the bottom of the bowl and pour in the water slowly until it is still and nearly full.
Scatter a tiny pinch of Mugwort on the surface and speak the chant softly over the water.
If the moon is hidden, light the candle in its holder on a heatproof dish behind you or to one side so its light touches the water but its flame is not reflected directly.
Breathe slowly, soften your gaze, and look into the water rather than at it, letting your eyes relax for ten to twenty minutes.
Notice any images, colors, words or feelings that come, without forcing them, and write them down right away.
When you are done, thank the moon and the water and snuff the candle.
howToUse: Read over your notes the next day and over the coming weeks; symbols often make sense later. Pour the water onto the earth, compost the Mugwort, and rinse and dry the stone. Keep the bowl only for divination, wrapped in a dark cloth between uses, and scry again at each full moon to build the skill.
chant:
Water dark and moonlight bright,
show me what is hid from sight.
Still the ripple, clear the glass;
let the truth before me pass.
intention: I open my inner sight and receive clear, truthful guidance from the still water.
timing: Full moon night; Monday (the moon's day).
bestTime: Any time of year; especially autumn and around Samhain
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Do not drink the scrying water. Mugwort can trigger allergies in people sensitive to ragweed, daisies or related plants, and should be avoided by anyone who is pregnant or breastfeeding, even in small amounts. Use only water-safe stones such as Moonstone or Amethyst; soft or porous stones like Selenite can dissolve or crack. If gazing leaves you dizzy or unsettled, stop, eat something and ground yourself. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the bowl, water and Mugwort where pets cannot drink or nibble them, and keep pets clear of the candle.

name: Pendulum Blessing and Attunement
description: Dowsing with a swinging weight or pendulum has been used in Europe for centuries to find water, lost things and answers to yes-or-no questions. Many practitioners believe a new pendulum works best after it is cleansed, blessed and 'taught' its owner's signals. This ritual cleanses your pendulum with Frankincense smoke and moonlight, dedicates it to truth, and attunes it so you know which swing means yes, no and maybe.

ingredients.item: Self-lighting charcoal disk and a heatproof censer filled with sand
Selenite plate or a clean white cloth

steps: Open a window to ventilate the room, then light the charcoal disk in the sand-filled censer and the white candle in its holder on a heatproof dish.
Place a few grains of Frankincense resin on the charcoal and pass the pendulum slowly through the smoke three times, saying, 'I cleanse you of all that came before.'
Hold the pendulum in both hands, breathe on it, and speak the chant to bless it and dedicate it to truth and the highest good.
Rest your elbow on the table, hold the chain lightly between thumb and finger, and say, 'Show me yes.' Note the motion, then repeat for 'Show me no' and 'Show me maybe' or 'I cannot answer.'
Draw the three motions on your paper and test them with a few questions you already know the answers to.
Lay the pendulum on the Selenite plate or white cloth on a windowsill under the moon overnight to rest and charge.
Make sure the charcoal is fully out, drown it in water once cool, and snuff the candle.
howToUse: Keep the pendulum in a pouch with your signal chart and check its signals again before important readings, as they can shift. Ask clear yes-or-no questions while calm and neutral. Cleanse it again with smoke or moonlight after heavy use or if its answers start to feel muddled. Pendulum work is for reflection, and is never a substitute for medical, legal or financial advice.
chant:
Swing of truth and steady thread,
by smoke and moon and candle fed,
show me only what is so;
yes and no I'll come to know.
intention: I bless and attune my pendulum to speak only truth for my highest good.
timing: Full moon or waxing moon; Monday or Wednesday.
bestTime: Any time of year
caution: Never leave a burning candle unattended or lit while you sleep; use a sturdy holder on a heatproof dish at least 12 inches from curtains, paper and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets. Burn charcoal and resin only with a window open and never in a small, closed room, as burning charcoal makes carbon monoxide; keep the censer on a heatproof surface filled with sand, and let the charcoal cool completely before drowning it and throwing it away. Incense smoke can irritate the lungs, so avoid it around people with asthma, infants and pet birds; moonlight alone works if you prefer no smoke. Hold the hot censer only by its handle. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep pets, especially birds, out of the room while the resin burns, and keep the charcoal and candle out of their reach.

name: Worry Stone Calm Charm
description: Worry stones, smooth stones with a thumb-sized hollow, are rubbed between the fingers to soothe restless hands and minds; similar pocket stones and touchstones are found in folk practice in Ireland, ancient Greece and elsewhere. This charm blesses a stone with a drop of diluted Lavender oil and a calming chant, so that each rub becomes a small spell for steadiness. It is meant to support, and never replace, medical or mental health care for stress or anxiety.

ingredients.item: Worry stone, or a smooth River Stone, Howlite or Rose Quartz palm stone
Jojoba Oil or Sweet Almond Oil
Small blue or green cloth pouch

steps: Wash the stone in cool water and dry it, saying, 'I wash away all worries that came before.'
In the small dish, mix one drop of Lavender Essential Oil into one teaspoon of Jojoba or Sweet Almond Oil, which is about a 1% dilution and safe for skin.
Dip a fingertip in the diluted oil and rub a tiny amount into the hollow of the stone.
Hold the stone in your palm and take four slow breaths: in for four counts, hold for four, out for four, hold for four.
Rub your thumb across the hollow slowly as you speak the chant three times.
Place the stone in its pouch and carry it with you.
howToUse: Whenever stress rises, take out the stone, rub the hollow slowly and repeat the four-count breathing and the chant, even silently. Re-anoint it with the diluted oil once a week, and rinse it under running water at each full moon to clear what it has absorbed. If worry or anxiety is affecting your sleep, work or daily life, please talk with a doctor or counselor; the stone can sit in your pocket alongside that help.
chant:
Smooth as water, still as stone,
I am steady, not alone.
Worry, rest beneath my thumb;
peace return and calm will come.
intention: I let my worries rest in this stone and return, again and again, to calm and steadiness.
timing: Any day; Monday for calm or Friday for comfort; waning moon to shrink worry.
bestTime: Any time of year
caution: This spell supports, and never replaces, medical or mental health care. Never use essential oils undiluted on the skin or swallow them; patch-test the diluted oil on your inner arm first and stop if redness or itching appears. Use Jojoba Oil instead of Sweet Almond Oil if you have a nut allergy. Keep the essential oil bottle and the small stone away from young children, as essential oils are poisonous if swallowed and small stones are a choking hazard. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Lavender and its essential oil are toxic to cats and can upset dogs; store the oil and the anointed stone out of pets' reach.

name: Seven-Night Lavender Sleep Sachet
description: Lavender has been tucked into linens and pillows across Europe for centuries for its clean scent and its reputation for bringing calm rest. Unlike a single charm, this sachet is worked over seven nights: each evening you tie one knot of rest into its ribbon and squeeze the sachet to wake its scent as part of a gentle wind-down routine. It supports good sleep habits and never replaces medical care for ongoing sleep problems.

ingredients.item: Linden flowers or Lemon Balm, dried
Small cotton or muslin drawstring bag

steps: In the bowl, mix the Lavender with the Linden or Lemon Balm, and the Hops if you are using them, stirring counterclockwise to slow the day's energy.
Hold your hands over the herbs and picture your bedroom dark, cool and quiet, and yourself sleeping deeply until morning.
Spoon the mixture into the bag, add the Amethyst if using, and pull the drawstring tight.
Each night for seven nights, about half an hour before bed, dim the lights and put away screens.
Squeeze the sachet gently, breathe in its scent three times, and tie one loose knot in the ribbon while speaking the chant.
Tuck the sachet inside your pillowcase or beside your pillow and lie down to rest.
On the seventh night, tie the seventh knot and leave the ribbon knotted around the sachet's neck to seal the charm.
howToUse: Keep the sachet by your pillow and squeeze it each night as your signal that the day is done. Refresh the herbs every month or when the scent fades, composting the old ones. Pair it with steady habits: a regular bedtime, a cool dark room and no caffeine late in the day. If you have trouble sleeping for more than a few weeks, snore loudly, or feel very tired in the daytime, see a doctor, as sleep problems can have medical causes.
chant:
Lavender and quiet night,
knot by knot I dim the light.
Seven times I'm wrapped in rest;
sleep come soft, and sleep come best.
intention: I invite deep, peaceful, restful sleep and wake refreshed each morning.
timing: Begin on a Monday evening during the waning moon and work for seven nights.
bestTime: Any time of year; especially the long nights of autumn and winter
caution: This spell supports, and never replaces, medical or mental health care. Some people are allergic to Lavender or other dried flowers; stop using the sachet if you notice sneezing, itching or a rash, and keep it out of the beds of babies and young children, whose sleep spaces should be kept bare. Use only dried herbs, not essential oil, on bedding, and never swallow the herbs. Hops can be sedating, so leave them out for anyone who is pregnant. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the sachet away from pets: Lavender is toxic to cats and can upset dogs, and Hops can cause a dangerous, sometimes fatal rise in body temperature in dogs, so leave the Hops out entirely if you have a dog.

name: Anniversary Remembrance Ribbon Spell
description: Anniversaries of a death, along with birthdays and holidays, can bring grief back sharply, even years later. Tying ribbons or strips of cloth to trees as prayers, wishes or remembrances is a folk custom found at holy wells and 'clootie' trees in Ireland and Scotland, and in many other places around the world. In this spell you write memories of your loved one on ribbons, bless them with Rosemary for remembrance, and tie them to a branch, giving your grief a gentle, loving place to go on a hard day.

ingredients.item: Cotton or other natural-fiber ribbons or fabric strips
Bare branch in a vase, or a tree in your own yard
Photo or keepsake of your loved one

steps: Set the photo or keepsake on a table with the glass of water beside it and the ribbons and Rosemary close at hand.
Hold the Rosemary sprigs, crush one leaf between your fingers and breathe in its scent, and say your loved one's name aloud.
On each ribbon, write one memory, a word they used to say, something you wish you could tell them, or a thank-you.
Brush each ribbon with the Rosemary, reading what you wrote aloud or silently, and let yourself cry if tears come.
Tie the ribbons one by one to the branch or tree, speaking the chant as you tie the last one.
Tuck a Rosemary sprig among the ribbons, drink the glass of water slowly as a small act of caring for yourself, and spend the rest of the day gently.
howToUse: Leave the ribbons on the branch for the anniversary week, then untie them and keep them in a box with the dried Rosemary to add to in years to come. If you tied them to a living tree, remove them within a few weeks so they do not harm the tree or tangle wildlife. Reach out to someone who also loved them, or to a grief counselor or support group; this spell supports, and never replaces, that care.
chant:
Ribbon, rosemary and thread,
hold the words I've left unsaid.
Love that's lost is never gone;
in my heart you travel on.
intention: I honor my loved one with tender memories and allow my grief to be held with love on this hard day.
timing: On or near the anniversary, birthday or any day grief feels heavy.
bestTime: Any time of year
caution: This spell supports, and never replaces, medical or mental health care. Grief can be overwhelming; if it is keeping you from daily life for a long time, or if you have thoughts of harming yourself, contact a doctor or counselor, or call or text 988 in the US (or your local emergency number). Tie ribbons only to trees you own or have permission to use, never so tight they bind the bark, and remove them afterward. Edible part: the glass of plain water only; the Rosemary is not to be eaten.
pets: Cats and dogs can swallow ribbon and string, which can cause dangerous intestinal blockages; keep the branch and loose ribbons out of their reach.

name: Hospital Stay and Surgery Protection Charm
description: Carrying a small blessed token, a holy medal, a written prayer or a stone from home, has comforted people through illness and surgery in many traditions. This gentle charm makes a simple, flame-free and scent-free pouch with a stone and a written blessing that can rest at the bedside, and a matching blessing that a loved one keeps at home. It is purely for comfort and spiritual support, and it supports, and never replaces, the medical care of your doctors and nurses.

ingredients.item: Clear Quartz or Rose Quartz tumbled stone
ingredients.amount: 2 (one for the patient, one for home)

ingredients.item: Small cloth pouch with a drawstring
Small slips of paper and a pen
Bay Laurel leaf, dried (for the home charm only)
Bowl of water with a pinch of salt
Flameless LED candle (for the home part)

steps: At home before the hospital stay, rinse both stones in the bowl of salt water and dry them, saying, 'Be clean, be strong, be kind.'
On each slip of paper write a short blessing, such as 'Safe hands, steady heart, gentle healing, home again,' and the patient's first name.
Hold both stones together with both slips and speak the chant three times, picturing the patient wrapped in calm blue light.
Fold one slip around one stone, tie it with the blue thread, and place it in the pouch for the patient to keep at the bedside.
Fold the second slip with the other stone and the Bay Laurel leaf and set it at home beside the LED candle, switching the light on during the surgery or on hard days.
On the day of surgery, give the pouch to a family member or tuck it in the patient's bag, since jewelry and personal items are usually removed before surgery.
howToUse: Keep the pouch on the bedside table or in a bag during the hospital stay, and hold it when you feel afraid. The loved one at home can hold the matching stone and say the chant at the time of surgery or each evening. When the patient is home again, rinse both stones, burn or bury the blessings with thanks (outdoors and safely) or keep them, and give the Bay Laurel leaf back to the earth.
chant:
Steady hands and gentle care,
safety held in every prayer.
Body mend and spirit rest;
home again, and safely blessed.
intention: I surround this hospital stay with calm, comfort and protection, and trust in good care and gentle healing.
timing: The day or evening before admission or surgery; any moon phase.
bestTime: Any time of year, whenever needed
caution: This spell supports, and never replaces, medical or mental health care. Follow every instruction from your medical team. Never bring candles, matches, lighters, incense or essential oils into a hospital: open flames are extremely dangerous near medical oxygen, and many patients are sensitive to scents. Leave herbs and plants out of the hospital pouch, as some units, such as intensive care, oncology and transplant units, do not allow plants or flowers for infection control; ask the nursing staff before bringing anything in. Expect to remove jewelry and personal items before surgery and hand the pouch to a family member. Nothing in this spell is to be eaten or drunk.
pets: Keep the home charm, salt water and Bay Laurel leaf away from pets; bay leaves can upset dogs' and cats' stomachs.
